No. 412 p717a.text: Por grandeza no entiendo solamente el tamaño de un objeto peculiar, sino la anchura de una perspectiva entera considerada como una sola pieza.

transcription.reason: The institutional viewer provides printed page images for chapter II; its available modern transcription covers a different chapter and Google Books complete OCR was unavailable. Maker read both pages of the 1804 print.
transcription.original_text: Por grandeza no entiendo solamente el tamaño de un objeto peculiar, sino la anchura de una perspectiva entera considerada como una sola pieza.

No. 412 p717a.alignment: Both sentences define greatness as the extent of an entire view as one piece in contrast to the size of a single object. The translation uses anchura, literally breadth, for the more general largeness; request independent assessment of this narrowing.
No. 412 p717a.page_span: Por grandeza no entiendo solamente el tamaño de un objeto peculiar, sino la anchura de una perspectiva entera considerada como una sola

No. 412 p717a.alignment: Read English p. 717 and Spanish pp. 33–34 against both independently fetched images. The Spanish preserves the contrast between the size of an individual object and the extent of a whole view considered as one piece. Anchura emphasizes breadth where largeness is more general, and peculiar can suggest a particular or distinctive object; in this context the whole-view definition remains aligned. Historical spelling and punctuation match the print, including pieza on p. 34.
